title: A Baby Hippo Named 'Breadroll' Is Stealing Hearts!
summary: What's small, round, and totally adorable? A baby pygmy hippo named Brötchen! That's German for "breadroll," and this little girl is quickly becoming everyone's favorite snack—well, not to eat, but to watch. Brötchen was born on May 9th at Zoo Berlin, weighing just 13 pounds. That's about as heavy as a big watermelon. But don't let her size fool you. When she grows up, she'll be as long as a sofa and weigh as much as a grand piano—up to 600 pounds! Pygmy hippos are like the smaller, shyer cousins of the huge hippos you see in cartoons. They love water because it keeps their skin from drying out. In fact, their skin makes a special pink goo that works like sunscreen and soap all in one. When keepers spray Brötchen with water, it foams up—not from soap, but from that natural goo! Brötchen is already a social media star, with thousands of likes on her photos. But here's the serious part: pygmy hippos are endangered. There are fewer than 2,500 adults left in the wild in West Africa. Their homes are being destroyed by mining and cutting down forests. So every new baby like Brötchen is a tiny hope for her whole species. The zoo says protecting them is more important than ever. Next time you see a cute animal video, remember: some of them need our help just to survive.
why_it_matters: When you share an adorable animal video, you might also be raising awareness about animals that need our protection, inspiring people to save their homes.

background_read: Pygmy hippos are much smaller and shyer than their huge relatives, the common hippopotamus. They live hidden in the rainforests and swamps of West Africa, a region that includes countries like Liberia and Sierra Leone.
Berlin Zoo (Germany's oldest zoo, opened in 1844) is a leader in protecting endangered animals by carefully breeding them, which helps keep their populations alive even if the wild ones disappear.
Gold and diamond mining, along with logging, have wiped out large parts of West African forests, leaving pygmy hippos with fewer places to hide and find food.
Article_Structure: WHO: A baby pygmy hippo nicknamed Brötchen (which means 'breadroll' in German), born at Zoo Berlin.
WHAT: She quickly became a social media sensation, with thousands of likes, and shows how cute a baby hippo can be.
WHERE: Zoo Berlin, the main zoo in the capital city of Germany.
WHY: Because pygmy hippos are endangered with fewer than 2,500 left in the wild, every newborn like Brötchen brings hope for the species' survival.

perspectives.description: People love watching baby animals and it makes them want to visit zoos, which can help fund protection programs for endangered species.
Some people argue that wild animals belong in their natural habitat, not in cages, and that protecting forests is better than breeding them in zoos.
Researchers study pygmy hippos in zoos to learn about their behavior, diet, and health, which can help create better conservation plans for the wild.
